answer: Clock-skew fingerprints. Every machine's quartz oscillator drifts by its own few ppm, so validators collect each seat's signed timestamps for 48 h and fit a skew line. Seats whose skews match within 0.1 ppm, an island of VMs on one host, merge into one vote. Separate hardware costs ~$120 per mini PC, so 500 fakes run $60k plus power, while an honest agent needs one box. A new seat's badge pigment stays grey until its skew is stable. Failure mode: software skew spoofing; check: random-interval pings cross-checked against network jitter.
